chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ibn Arafah, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has in every day and night a caller who calls out: “Restraint, restraint, O servants of Allah, from acts of disobedience to Allah.”
So were it not for grazing animals, nursing children, and elderly ones bowed in worship, the punishment would surely be poured down upon you in a pouring, crushing you with a crushing.

key_terms.بَهَائِمُ: animals whose presence is mentioned as a cause for mercy being maintained
key_terms.مَعَاصِي: acts of disobedience and sins against Allah
key_terms.مُنَادِيًا: a caller appointed to call out a warning

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain why Allah’s punishment may be delayed despite widespread sins?
ai.summary: This hadith warns people continually against disobedience to Allah, describing a divine call repeated every day and night. It also teaches that Allah’s punishment is held back from people due to the presence of innocent and worshipful beings among them, highlighting both divine mercy and the grave consequence of persistent sin.
